title: Earnings Season Kickoff, Bank Earnings & Nvidia China Greenlight - The Friday Market Wrap!
summary: Eisman uses the first earnings week to demonstrate thesis checking and bank valuation. He compares tangible-equity returns across major banks, distinguishes earnings beats from stock reactions, and explains his move from GFC bearishness to a predominantly long US portfolio. Corporate observations are contemporaneous diagnoses, not newly successful forecasts.
assessment: His best contribution is relating bank profitability to valuation while explicitly acknowledging exceptions. The stronger claims about permanent safety, unique US technology exposure and Citi never recovering an old price are not precise, finite predictions. Earnings-season evidence supports resilience but does not make tariffs the only possible risk.
framework_points: Use earnings to test a thesis rather than guess the next trading-day reaction.
Compare sustainable ROTCE with price to tangible book, then explain exceptions.
Separate recurring income from reserve releases and investment gains.
Update a market stance when bank leverage and the opportunity set change.
tools_and_charts: Sector weights including reclassified technology businesses
transcript_cautions: Reported and adjusted earnings are mixed in the narration; the audit uses each issuer definition.
The narrated bank table is discussed as a tool, not claimed as an independently captured chart.
Personal medical details are outside the material investment-claim scope.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: Allowing Nvidia H20 exports signals a more selective China technology policy.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track actual licenses, shipments and the broader export-control schedule.
claims.reason: A license decision can change while other controls persist. One product exception does not establish a durable policy regime.
claims.next_check: Track actual licenses, shipments and the broader export-control schedule.

claims.claim: Strong earnings do not guarantee a positive immediate stock reaction because expectations and positioning matter.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare results with dated expectations and changes in forward estimates.
claims.reason: Price reflects expected future cash flows and risk, not only the reported growth rate. A positive result can still fall short of expectations.
claims.next_check: Compare results with dated expectations and changes in forward estimates.

assumptions: Prices incorporate some expectations before results
proof.derivation: If investors expected a larger increase in future cash flows than the announcement supports, the estimate of value can fall even when reported earnings rise.

claims.claim: Higher sustainable tangible-equity returns generally justify a higher tangible-book multiple.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare normalized returns, cost of equity, growth and capital requirements.
claims.reason: A residual-income model links value above book to future returns exceeding the required return, holding risk and growth assumptions comparable. The observed relationship need not be exact.
claims.next_check: Compare normalized returns, cost of equity, growth and capital requirements.

assumptions: Returns are sustainable rather than a one-quarter spike
proof.derivation: Value equals book plus the discounted value of future income above the equity charge. Higher sustainable return on the same equity base raises residual income and justified price/book.

claims.claim: JPMorgan combines high tangible-equity profitability with strong trading and investment banking.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare consistently defined returns and revenue by business.
claims.reason: The dated issuer report supports the operating description. Best in the business is read relative to the named large-bank peer group, not every financial institution worldwide.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Reported ROTCE was 21%, with strong markets revenue. This is a dated profitability observation, not a stock-return forecast.

claims.next_check: Compare consistently defined returns and revenue by business.

claims.claim: The Wells Fargo asset cap constrained growth and its removal will not produce an immediate smooth recovery.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate cap restrictions from pricing, funding and reserve-release effects.
claims.reason: The cap and uneven net-interest performance are real. Attributing the entire NII shortfall to the cap is too strong because rates, deposit mix and other balance-sheet choices also matter.

evidence.title: Wells Fargo Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: The bank reported 15.2% ROTCE and weaker year-over-year net interest income. Rate, deposit and balance-sheet mix effects accompany the legacy asset-cap constraint.

evidence.title: Wells Fargo asset-growth restriction removed
evidence.finding: The Fed removed the asset-growth restriction after required remediation. Other provisions of the enforcement action remained in place.

claims.next_check: Separate cap restrictions from pricing, funding and reserve-release effects.

claims.claim: Citi is improving but its low ROTCE explains a valuation discount to stronger peers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track normalized profitability and tangible-book valuation over the turnaround.
claims.reason: The 8.7% return and improving revenue support the profitability comparison. Risk, growth and restructuring credibility also affect the multiple.

evidence.title: Citi Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Reported ROTCE was 8.7%; revenue grew 8%. Improving operations did not yet produce peer-leading profitability.

claims.next_check: Track normalized profitability and tangible-book valuation over the turnaround.

claims.claim: Citi will never again reach its split-adjusted pre-crisis stock-price peak.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use an explicit horizon and split-adjusted total-return benchmark.
claims.reason: Never has no finite verification date, and nominal prices can change with future splits and inflation. Past dilution does not mathematically impose a permanent price ceiling.
claims.next_check: Use an explicit horizon and split-adjusted total-return benchmark.

claims.claim: BlackRock headline earnings can look better than the underlying flow picture because investment income is less repeatable.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate investment gains, long-term flows, low-fee redemptions and organic base-fee growth.
claims.reason: This is a sensible quality-of-earnings distinction, but the episode attribution to one institutional withdrawal requires matched issuer flow data and fee rates.
claims.next_check: Separate investment gains, long-term flows, low-fee redemptions and organic base-fee growth.

claims.claim: Goldman benefits from volatility and a recovery in M&A, but its return profile still lags the strongest peers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare markets and advisory revenue, capital usage and normalized ROTCE.
claims.reason: The mechanism and comparison are plausible, but a full like-for-like peer reconciliation is needed to score the exact operating diagnosis.
claims.next_check: Compare markets and advisory revenue, capital usage and normalized ROTCE.

claims.claim: Morgan Stanley earns a valuation premium partly because wealth management contributes durable profits.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare fee persistence, capital intensity and segment returns.
claims.reason: Eisman explicitly admits uncertainty about why its multiple exceeds JPMorgan. The business mix hypothesis is not presented as established causality.
claims.next_check: Compare fee persistence, capital intensity and segment returns.

claims.claim: M&T and PNC show solid profitability without a visible broad credit deterioration.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect non-accruals, charge-offs, reserve coverage and return definitions.
claims.reason: The quarter is a limited observation. Credit losses, provision releases and normalized returns need a consistent peer table to resolve the claim fully.
claims.next_check: Inspect non-accruals, charge-offs, reserve coverage and return definitions.

claims.claim: Bank of America legacy low-yield bond purchases constrain its earnings and tangible-equity returns.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Decompose asset yields, deposit costs, balances and securities maturities.
claims.reason: Low-yield assets can depress relative earnings, and the reported return was 13.4%. Yet NII was already growing; unrealized losses are not themselves the full explanation of a revenue miss.

evidence.title: Bank of America Q2 2025 presentation
evidence.finding: ROTCE was 13.4%. Net interest income rose from the preceding quarter and year; low-yielding legacy assets were not equivalent to an immediate insolvency conclusion.

claims.next_check: Decompose asset yields, deposit costs, balances and securities maturities.

claims.claim: Valuation anomalies can reflect expectations for future normalization rather than current-quarter returns.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare implied future returns with analyst and management forecasts.
claims.reason: A valuation model depends on future income rather than a mechanical capitalization of one quarter. The specific motives of marginal investors remain unobserved.
claims.next_check: Compare implied future returns with analyst and management forecasts.

assumptions: Equity value discounts expected future distributions
proof.derivation: Two firms with equal current earnings can have different value if expected growth, risk or future margins differ. Current-quarter ROTCE alone cannot determine the price/book multiple.

claims.claim: Progressive is an exceptionally strong insurance franchise.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare underwriting profitability, growth, reserves and capital through a full cycle.
claims.reason: Best on the planet is a qualitative ranking without a common risk-adjusted benchmark or horizon.
claims.next_check: Compare underwriting profitability, growth, reserves and capital through a full cycle.

claims.claim: A slow pharmaceutical tariff phase-in matters because domestic plants cannot be created overnight.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare announced tariffs with validated production-transfer schedules.
claims.reason: The timing mechanism is plausible, but company-specific capacity, qualification and regulatory lead times are required to quantify the benefit.
claims.next_check: Compare announced tariffs with validated production-transfer schedules.

claims.claim: GE breakup and aviation demand have produced strong Aerospace operating performance.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track service revenue, engine deliveries, margins and cash conversion separately.
claims.reason: The issuer reported strong adjusted revenue, profit and cash growth. The earnings release supports performance, while not isolating how much was caused by the breakup.

evidence.title: GE Aerospace Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Adjusted revenue rose 23% and adjusted EPS rose 38%; guidance increased. Services volume and pricing contributed, not only new aircraft production.

claims.next_check: Track service revenue, engine deliveries, margins and cash conversion separately.

claims.claim: Higher medical costs are compressing health-insurer earnings and forcing guidance cuts.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare medical cost trends, pricing, membership mix and adjusted guidance.
claims.reason: This sector diagnosis needs plan-mix and medical-loss-ratio evidence rather than revenue growth alone. The transcript specifies an Elevance guidance cut but no independent sector-wide counterfactual.
claims.next_check: Compare medical cost trends, pricing, membership mix and adjusted guidance.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola switching to cane sugar threatens high-fructose-corn-syrup suppliers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the precise product announcement and subsequent ingredient purchases.
claims.reason: A product addition is not necessarily a replacement of the full US formulation. Actual volume substitution and supplier exposure are needed.
claims.next_check: Compare the precise product announcement and subsequent ingredient purchases.

claims.claim: Netflix strong growth can coexist with a falling stock when expectations are already high.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare dated expectations, guidance and valuation with the actual reaction.
claims.reason: The general mechanism is valid, but the claimed whisper-number explanation for that day is explicitly a guess.
claims.next_check: Compare dated expectations, guidance and valuation with the actual reaction.

claims.claim: A viable Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern deal could signal a much more permissive M&A environment.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track regulatory decisions, deal completions and broad transaction activity.
claims.reason: A contemplated bid is not an approval, and one sector transaction does not establish a general merger wave.
claims.next_check: Track regulatory decisions, deal completions and broad transaction activity.

claims.claim: The economy and bank credit look sound, with trade war the major risk to the outlook.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track credit, employment, demand and policy shocks beyond the selected earnings sample.
claims.reason: Large-bank stress results support resilience under modeled conditions. They do not establish economy-wide safety or make trade policy the only possible downside.

evidence.title: 2025 stress-test results
evidence.finding: All 22 tested large banks remained above minimum capital requirements in the modeled severe scenario.

claims.next_check: Track credit, employment, demand and policy shocks beyond the selected earnings sample.

claims.claim: The US offers uniquely large technology exposure and is therefore his preferred investment market.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare investable weights and expected returns using common definitions.
claims.reason: This is a portfolio preference using an expansive technology definition. A cross-country claim requires consistent classification, and valuation still matters.
claims.next_check: Compare investable weights and expected returns using common definitions.

claims.claim: Post-GFC bank deleveraging changed his view from systemic bearishness to confidence in banking resilience.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare capital, liquidity and asset risks across regimes.
claims.reason: The stress-test evidence supports greater current resilience. It does not validate an absolute guarantee of safety or the stated personal performance record.

evidence.title: 2025 stress-test results
evidence.finding: All 22 tested large banks remained above minimum capital requirements in the modeled severe scenario.

claims.next_check: Compare capital, liquidity and asset risks across regimes.

claims.claim: A recession will expose private-credit weaknesses, but private credit will not cause the recession.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify the recession, credit-loss measure and causal ordering.
claims.reason: The view is conditional and lacks a defined systemic-loss threshold. He explicitly says data are insufficient for a firm bubble conclusion.
claims.next_check: Specify the recession, credit-loss measure and causal ordering.

claims.claim: AI, industrial investment and broader economic dynamism justify a long-term bullish US equity stance.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify investable exposure, valuation and a return horizon.
claims.reason: The structural thesis is clear but has no entry valuation, horizon or benchmark-relative target. It should not be scored as a continuously renewed short-term prediction.
claims.next_check: Specify investable exposure, valuation and a return horizon.
